# ALS evidence packet — draft v1

This curated input is not a comprehensive review. Every method receives the same UTF-8 file. Summaries are original paraphrases. Bibliographic metadata and abstracts were checked through the public NCBI ID converter and PubMed EFetch on 2026-10-05. Selected studies predate 2025; this does not remove knowledge already in a model's training. Co-Scientist outputs are not included.

## Research question

Propose one specific, testable hypothesis connecting phosphorylation of a nuclear-pore-complex nucleoporin to ALS-related neuronal dysfunction. Explain the causal chain, distinguish an initiating mechanism from a downstream response, and propose an experimental strategy that discriminates the hypothesis from an alternative. Identify supported premises, speculative bridges, and a falsifying observation. This adapts Co-Scientist Supplementary Note 10; nucleoporin phosphorylation is not supplied as an established ALS cause.

## S1 — TDP-43 and nuclear-pore dysfunction

Chou et al. (2018), *TDP-43 pathology disrupts nuclear pore complexes and nucleocytoplasmic transport in ALS/FTD*. Nature Neuroscience. DOI: `10.1038/s41593-017-0047-3`; PMID: `29311743`; PMCID: `PMC5800968`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29311743/).

Nuclear-pore and transport components were associated with insoluble TDP-43 aggregates. Disease-linked TDP-43 disrupted nucleoporin localization and nuclear transport in experimental cell systems; relevant pore pathology was observed in ALS tissue. This supports examining the connection between TDP-43 pathology and transport disruption. It does not identify a nucleoporin phosphorylation event as the initiating cause or establish the same sequence in every ALS subtype.

## S2 — C9orf72-associated transport defects

Zhang et al. (2015), *The C9orf72 repeat expansion disrupts nucleocytoplasmic transport*. Nature. DOI: `10.1038/nature14973`; PMID: `26308891`; PMCID: `PMC4800742`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26308891/).

Expanded C9orf72 repeat RNA was linked to altered RanGAP localization and impaired nuclear import in models and patient-derived neurons. Manipulations of transport or repeat-RNA-associated mechanisms modified model phenotypes. This supplies a genetic-context-specific route to transport dysfunction. It does not show that sporadic ALS arises by the same route or directly establish a nucleoporin phosphorylation mechanism.

## S3 — A stress-granule-independent route

Gasset-Rosa et al. (2019), *Cytoplasmic TDP-43 De-mixing Independent of Stress Granules Drives Inhibition of Nuclear Import, Loss of Nuclear TDP-43, and Cell Death*. Neuron. DOI: `10.1016/j.neuron.2019.02.038`; PMID: `30853299`; PMCID: `PMC6548321`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30853299/).

Persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies could form independently of conventional stress granules. They recruited or mislocalized transport-associated proteins and were associated with impaired transport, nuclear TDP-43 depletion, and cell death. Phosphorylated TDP-43 accumulated in these assemblies. That is not itself evidence of nucleoporin phosphorylation. The experimental perturbations do not establish that every physiological ALS trajectory begins in this way.

## S4 — A stress-granule-associated route

Zhang et al. (2018), *Stress Granule Assembly Disrupts Nucleocytoplasmic Transport*. Cell. DOI: `10.1016/j.cell.2018.03.025`; PMID: `29628143`; PMCID: `PMC6083872`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29628143/).

Cellular stress recruited transport factors into stress granules and impaired nucleocytoplasmic transport. Altering stress-granule assembly modified transport defects and disease-model phenotypes. This provides a sequestration-based alternative to an intrinsic pore-modification hypothesis. Read alongside S3, it does not justify assuming that conventional stress granules are required for every TDP-43-associated transport defect.

## Evidence boundaries

- These selected passages do not establish that nucleoporin phosphorylation initiates ALS. Label a proposed kinase, modification site, or interaction as an assumption unless a supplied source supports it.
- Specify the ALS context; do not assume a universal mechanism across genetic and sporadic disease.
- Distinguish pore alteration, transport-factor sequestration, and failure secondary to broader stress.
- Explain temporal and perturbational evidence that would distinguish cause from consequence.
- Propose a research hypothesis rather than claiming a mechanism or treatment has been validated.


Proposed answer (the answer to evaluate):
CDK5-dependent NUP98 phosphorylation initiates nuclear-import failure in TARDBP-mutant motor neurons

Hypothesis and evidence. In TARDBP p.M337V spinal motor neurons, CDK5-dependent NUP98 phosphorylation reduces pore residence, initiating import failure before persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies. Impaired TDP-43 import then causes nuclear depletion and neuronal dysfunction. Initiation refers to transport failure downstream of this allele, not ALS generally. TDP-43-associated pore disruption [S1], stress-granule-independent assembly-associated import inhibition [S3], and stress-granule sequestration [S4] support transport-focused investigation. C9orf72-associated RanGAP/import defects supply a genetically distinct alternative [S2]. Phosphorylated TDP-43 [S3] is not evidence of phosphorylated NUP98. Mutant-linked CDK5 activation, physiological CDK5–NUP98 coupling, and displacement impairing receptor transit are speculative bridges. Neuronal CDK5, phosphorylation-sensitive NUP98 residence, and this allele’s ALS association are unverified prior knowledge. Comparison with [S1]–[S4] identifies a substrate-specific initiating proposal, but supplies no evidence prioritizing this pair. A broader focused CDK5–NUP98 prior-art check remains necessary; literature-wide novelty is unestablished.

Substrate qualification. Use patient-derived p.M337V iPSCs, isogenic corrections, and reciprocal knock-ins in two unrelated backgrounds. Freeze one endogenous NUP98 residue or inseparable cluster only if occupancy rises before import failure, acute CDK5 degradation lowers it before stress changes, and active—but not inactive—CDK5 add-back restores it. Require validated CDK5-selective phosphate tracing to endogenous NUP98 in neurons alongside purified-substrate assays; tracing feasibility and specificity are assumptions. Motifs or purified phosphorylation alone cannot establish physiological kinase attribution. If no site qualifies, stop rather than substitute another candidate.

Temporal precedence. Begin before detectable abnormalities; collect 30-minute single-cell imaging for seven days and six-hour matched phosphoproteomics. A nonperturbing, occupancy-calibrated phosphosite sensor is required for same-cell ordering. Before genotype unblinding, freeze detection limits and false-negative rates using calibrated controls. Require phosphorylation, residence loss, import slowing, and nuclear depletion in that order, separated by at least two frames, without detectable assemblies or preceding generalized ATP/stress deterioration. Unresolved ordering or abnormalities at baseline cannot establish initiation. Track both assembly classes, export, permeability, and turnover. Endogenous TDP-43 photoactivation with compartmental fitting distinguishes import failure from increased export, reduced retention, or degradation.

Necessity, sufficiency, and mediation. Compare endogenous phospho-null edits with precise revertants, requiring normal baseline pores/import. Early import kinetics are primary; protection should precede measured stress improvement. Inducible NUP98-localized active CDK5 at mutant-matched occupancy tests sufficiency against inactive, untargeted, and phospho-null controls while monitoring neighboring phosphorylation. To test displacement as mediator, use a function-validated, phosphorylation-independent pore tether with matched controls: import should recover while CDK5 activity and NUP98 phosphorylation persist. Separately restore nuclear TDP-43 abundance and function to corrected-cell levels using a validated retention tool while phosphorylation, displacement, and generic import failure persist. Apply rescues before functional decline. Improved electrophysiology and survival support downstream mediation; failed selective rescue challenges the corresponding link rather than being explained by temporal precedence alone.

Alternative discrimination. Use phosphosite-state × conventional-granule-suppression × persistent-assembly-suppression factorials. G3BP1/2 interference targets conventional granules; test a cytoplasmic TDP-43 intrabody and engineered Hsp104(A503V) separately as persistent-assembly candidates. G3BP1/2 and Hsp104 rationales are unverified prior knowledge; selectivity is unestablished. Include re-expression, nonbinding, and catalytic-dead controls. In both genotypes, including assembly-free mutant windows, reject interventions causing assembly-independent changes in soluble TDP-43 abundance, mobility/function, CDK5 activity, phosphorylation, pore localization, import, or ATP/stress. Predefine successful suppression as at least 95% burden reduction and fewer than 5% assembly-positive neurons for each targeted class; analyze assembly-negative trajectories against calibrated detection limits. Phosphosite-dependent failure persisting when both classes meet these criteria favors intrinsic pore alteration. Rescue while phosphorylation persists favors sequestration. Conventional-granule suppression alone cannot exclude [S3]. Without mutant-validated selectivity, discrimination remains unresolved.

Falsification and limitations. Reproducible import failure preceding phosphorylation, or persistent early import failure despite verified modification elimination in otherwise functional phospho-null neurons, falsifies the initiating chain. Assembly elimination restoring import despite maintained phosphorylation undermines proposed sufficiency. Immature neurons, subthreshold assemblies, sensor/tether/retention artifacts, neighboring kinase substrates, and residual pleiotropy constrain interpretation. Engineered tracing, sensors, and rescues require validation; missing prerequisites yield inconclusive results, not support. Positive findings would support an allele-specific preclinical mechanism, not universal ALS causation or a validated treatment.

Ranked proposal:
CDK5-dependent NUP98 phosphorylation initiates nuclear-import failure in TARDBP-mutant motor neurons
